statusNote: TIER-2-FINAL (2026-07-24; enforcement amended 2026-07-25): reviewed identities are exact blob bytes or anchored generator regions. Derived closure files and their digest remain diagnostic provenance; unrelated edits outside a reviewed region do not require re-banking. Region identity, consumer set, resolver row, verifier chain and the completed  disposition remain enforced exactly. pendingClassification empty; no tracked-to-zero residue. Any reviewed identity change requires -governed separate architect/security approval.
scopeRule: A carve-out admits the reviewed guard IMPLEMENTATION (exact body or narrow reviewed generator), never the interface/signature grammar around it — declaration/ABI/signature syntax is Tier-2 typed-table territory, not a trust object.

entries.purpose: The reviewed M-of-N threshold-quorum acceptance guard body (S2 lowering ): on-chain acceptance of attested evidence requires M distinct authorized observer signatures.
entries.threatBoundary: Acceptance forgery: a coordination leg firing on unattested or under-quorum evidence, or on signatures from unauthorized observers.
entries.whyNotDeclarative: A reviewed, security-audited verbatim body; templating it per-construct would fragment the audited unit and weaken review ( registry contract, form 1).

entries.artifact: lib/backends/postgres/model/PostgresModel.cpp (single-policy accept_<proc> quorum guard generation into PgProcedure.functions)
entries.parameterSurface: Closed, semantically typed: canonical procedure id, declared key ref, closed type mapping, canonical observer-set id, bounded threshold M<=N. Raw target fragments / SQL identifiers are unrepresentable.
entries.purpose: Generates the per-procedure accept_<proc> M-of-N quorum acceptance function (specialized per procedure, one reviewed shape).
entries.threatBoundary: Evidence acceptance forgery in the database rail; per-procedure specialization must not open an injection or shape-drift surface.
entries.whyNotDeclarative: Per-procedure specialization over a closed typed parameter surface ( registry contract, form 2) — the anchored region hash + independent output verifier make each variant exactly enumerable.

entries.artifact: lib/backends/postgres/model/PostgresModel.cpp (the  accept_ REVOKE trailer, fail-closed RawSql; printPostgres is the sole authorized sink)
entries.parameterSurface: The exact generated accept_<proc> signature (function name + argument type list) — nothing else.
entries.purpose: REVOKE EXECUTE ... FROM PUBLIC on the exact matching accept_<proc> overload: PUBLIC-callable acceptance is forgeable, so the guard is closed by default and GRANTed only to the aggregator role.
entries.threatBoundary: Privilege bypass: a PUBLIC caller invoking the acceptance entry point directly.
entries.whyNotDeclarative: The hardening property is keyed to the generated signature of its guard variant; it is one reviewed trailer, not a per-construct template.

entries.artifact: lib/backends/postgres/model/PostgresModel.cpp (temporal accept_ variant; signature carries the extra p_policy argument)
entries.parameterSurface: As PG-QUORUM-SINGLE plus the closed per-policy axis (canonical policy id); raw fragments unrepresentable.
entries.purpose: Generates the temporal (per-policy) quorum acceptance variant.
entries.threatBoundary: As PG-QUORUM-SINGLE, plus cross-policy confusion (accepting under the wrong policy's quorum).
entries.whyNotDeclarative: Same reviewed-generator rationale; distinct finalized semantic shape (single vs per-policy is a core decision,  finalized kinds).

entries.purpose: The  on-chain execution-claim digest: a domain-separated SHA-256 with explicit big-endian length framing over coordination identity + workflow key + the declared typed payload — reproduced byte-for-byte from the target-neutral reference (lib/spec-contract/CoordinationEnvelope.cpp), so acceptance of one payload never authorizes a different payload on the same key.
entries.threatBoundary: Claim/payload substitution: an accepted execution claim being used to authorize a DIFFERENT payload on the same workflow key; any cross-implementation divergence of the digest preimage silently splitting what each rail believes was accepted.
entries.whyNotDeclarative: A hand-authored, security-reviewed cryptographic canonicalization that must remain byte-equivalent across three implementations (C++ reference, Solidity, SQL) and is pinned to a committed cross-implementation vector; generating or templating it would fragment the audited unit and the equivalence proof ( registry contract, form 1).
entries.approvingDecision: (reviewed reference + cross-implementation vector) +  classification 2026-07-24 (final sign-off pending post- re-enumeration)

entries.purpose: The SQL realization of the  execution-claim digest (neu_frame + neu_execution_claim): the same framed SHA-256 preimage as the reference, computed in the database rail.
entries.threatBoundary: As SOL-EXECUTION-ENVELOPE: claim/payload substitution and cross-implementation preimage divergence.
entries.whyNotDeclarative: Same reviewed cross-implementation cryptographic canonicalization; byte-equivalence to the reference and the committed vector is the security property — not a layout idiom.

trackedToZero.disposition: COMPLETED (verified 2026-07-24): the three table shapes are migrated to typed .td nodes — defined in PostgresTargetNodes.td with generated printer handlers (PostgresTargetNodes.inc / PostgresPrinterHandlers.inc). The remaining `PgSchemaDecl(Kind::X, {})` factory calls are the legitimate typed instantiation of GENERATED nodes, not handwritten residue;  does not (and need not) remove them. No absence-probe residue remains on this axis.

prohibitions: No directory wildcards, prose-only exceptions, or per-domain/per-construct entries.

The projection core/graph never names a backend implementation ID (SOL-*/PG-* in core is a  violation); the per-target resolver maps (governedTarget, finalizedPrimitiveKind) to exactly ONE entry — zero or multiple matches fail.
Idiom tables carry no registry ID and perform no selection; a table may only lay out already-resolved output.
Adding or changing an entry (including any identity hash) requires -governed separate architect/security approval — never an implementation-slice edit.
